images.filename: Efficient Recovery Act Work Leads to $6 Million in Savings (7631913772).jpg
images.caption:
Workers begin demolishing LANL Building 21-2 at TA-21 at LANL in late July 2011.
Efficient contracting and waste management has led to a $6 million cost savings for a $73 million American Recovery and Reinvestment Project at Los Alamos National Laboratory (LANL).

The  savings has allowed for two additional large buildings to be added to the demolition schedule at LANL’s Technical Area 21 (TA-21). The $73 million in Recovery Act funds was already providing for the demolition of 22 buildings.

images.filename: Construction Begins on New Waste Processing Facility (7609873936).jpg
images.caption:
Construction has begun on a new facility that will help Los Alamos National Laboratory accelerate the shipment of transuranic (TRU) waste stored in large boxes  at Technical Area 54, Area G.

The new facility will allow the Lab to repackage boxes as large as 25 feet long that contain TRU waste from as long ago as the 1970s.

images.filename: A Safe End to Cold War Facilities (7507781830).jpg
images.caption:
The demolition of 24 buildings at Technical Area 21 at Los Alamos National Laboratory was completed six months ahead of schedule.

Few buildings remain at what was once a bustling research complex at Los Alamos National Laboratory’s Technical Area 21 (TA-21). The site that once housed 39 buildings is now mostly a smoothly graded mesa.

images.filename: 17 mCi Ac-225(NO3)3 at ORNL by Dr Andrew R Burgoyne.jpg
images.caption: Actinium-225 is produced by the Tri-Lab effort (Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Brookhaven National Laboratory and Los Alamos National Laboratory) for the US DOE Isotope Program.
